CLIHTF Landlord Notices
Important November 2026 Notice
As we approach the end of 2026 and prepare for the new year, the Chicago Low-Income Housing Trust Fund (CLIHTF) would like to share several important program updates and reminders. Please take a moment to review the following information regarding payment procedures, policy changes, rent increases, and compliance requirements to help ensure a smooth transition into 2027.
1.) GETTING PAID BY TIPALTI: From November 16, the one-time code you use to sign in to Tipalti may arrive in WhatsApp instead of by text message. It will come from a Tipalti phone number and show Tipalti as the sender. How you sign in doesn't change. Only enter the code on the Tipalti sign-in page, and don't share it with anyone, including anyone who says they're from Tipalti.
2.) SRO units and apartments with more than two bedrooms are now exempt from CLIHTF’s Attrition Policy.
3.) If you received approval of a 2027 rent increase, remember the new rent does not take effect until each lease renews sometime in 2027. If you don’t know whether or not your 2027 Annual Rent Increase request was approved, please contact your Program Specialist.
4.) Strive to provide updated Exhibit I/1-I-2 Tenant Income Verification forms with proof of income documentation (POI) sixty (60) days before lease renewal. Also please remember we give staff thirty (30) days to review new leases and POI so submitting early is the best way to get paid by CLIHTF on time!
5.) Landlords in compliance with CLIHTF requirements are eligible for first quarter 2027 payments under the 2026 Rental Subsidy Agreement (RSA). We begin accepting payment requests on December 1, 2026.
The earliest we can pay first quarter 2027 subsidies on properties for which all 2026 inspections, leases and POI is current is January 8, 2027.
As we enter this season of giving thanks, please know we are thankful for you working with us to provide affordable housing in Chicago to the working poor as well as families exiting homelessness. We couldn’t do this without you!

CLIHTF Escalation Process
Purpose:
The purpose of this escalation policy is to establish a clear procedure for handling unresolved issues or concerns that require escalating to higher levels of authority within the organization.
Procedure
1. Call/Contact your Program Specialist:
When a call or contact is made to the Program Specialist, the expected response time is within 48 business hours.
If the Program Specialist does not respond within the specified timeframe, the issue should be escalated to the RHSP Manager.
2. Call/Contact to Director of Program Operations:
If the Program Specialist does not respond within 24 business hours, the issue should be escalated to the Director of Program Operations
The expected response time for the Director of Program Operations is within a reasonable timeframe based on the urgency and nature of the issue. If the Director of Program Operation does not respond or the issue remains unresolved, the final escalation step is to contact the Executive Director
3. Call/Contact to Executive Director:
If the Director of Program Operations does not respond or the issue remains unresolved, the Executive Director should may be contacted.
The Executive Director will review the escalated issue and take appropriate action to address and resolve the matter.
Note: This escalation policy is designed to provide a structured approach for resolving concerns and maintaining accountability within CLIHTF.
